language.script_notes: Chilean Spanish as national; German-immigrant heritage visible in place names and some architecture around the Lake District (Puerto Varas, Frutillar), similar to Argentina's Bariloche.
false_friends: Argentine Patagonia (same mountains/glaciers, opposite side of the Andes)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: As national; more common on winding mountain/coastal roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: As national, though many roads are unpaved (ripio) in the remote far south.
road_furniture.curb_style: Minimal outside towns; the Carretera Austral is a famous, partly unpaved long-distance route through the region.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national; ferry terminal signage common given the fjord-broken coastline requires boat travel between road sections.

architecture.roof_style: Steep-pitched roofs in the German-influenced Lake District towns (Puerto Varas, Frutillar), reflecting both climate and heritage; simple utilitarian buildings further south.
architecture.roof_material: Wood shingle and metal roofing in the Lake District; corrugated metal on remote southern buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Alpine/German-influenced timber chalet architecture around the Lake District's volcanic lakes; isolated sheep estancias further south toward the Strait of Magellan; minimal development in the fjord-cut far south.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Warm wood tones in the Lake District's German-heritage towns; weathered, muted tones on remote southern buildings.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: German-influenced Lake District architecture with volcanic-lake backdrops (Osorno Volcano); isolated Patagonian sheep estancias; almost no dense urban development south of Puerto Montt; glacier and national park infrastructure (Torres del Paine).

nature.vegetation: Lush temperate (Valdivian) rainforest around the Lake District, transitioning to sparser subantarctic vegetation and eventually near-treeless terrain in the far south; forest gives way to ice fields and glaciers.
nature.terrain: A dramatic, deeply fjord-cut Pacific coastline, snow-capped volcanoes and lakes in the north of the region (Lake District), and vast glaciers, ice fields and jagged peaks (Torres del Paine) further south; the Andes narrow and merge with the coast.
nature.climate_signature: Cool, wet, and green in the Lake District; increasingly cold, windswept and glacier-dominated further south — a visually dramatic, often overcast look throughout.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: 4WD vehicles more common given unpaved roads (ripio) and rugged terrain, especially along the Carretera Austral.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Coverage concentrated along the Pan-American Highway north of Puerto Montt and the partial Carretera Austral further south.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Sparse south of Puerto Montt — the fjord-broken geography limits road (and therefore Street View) coverage significantly.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Andes mountains, glaciers and Lake District terrain straddling the same border region
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chilean Patagonia sits on the wetter Pacific side with denser rainforest and dramatic fjords; Argentine Patagonia sits on the drier eastern steppe side with Ruta 40's long straight gravel stretches and its own black-car Gen 3 coverage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Visually similar glacier-carved fjord coastline and mountain scenery
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chile has Spanish signage and right-hand traffic with Chilean plates; Norway has Norwegian signage and different road furniture entirely — context and any visible text resolve this quickly.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The south is lush temperate rainforest, fjords and glaciers; the north is barren desert, and Central Chile is Mediterranean vineyard country — all visually distinct.
